confirmed.claim: `variant="outline"` is not the installed glass-ui Button API and becomes dead intent.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED with hard proof. Live source `/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:8` and `:22` pass `variant="outline"`. The installed producer API `/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:6-18` declares `ButtonProps` with NO `variant` member — the axes are `emphasis` ("primary"|"secondary"|"quiet"|"text"), `tone`, `size`, `iconOnly`, `loading`. glass-ui 7.0.0 (package.json:83). The producer explicitly repudiates the name at `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/_shared/axes.d.ts:16`: "The tone axis ... NEVER a `variant` member." The compiled Button (`node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js:8-32`) has NO `inheritAttrs:!1` and styles purely off `data-emphasis`/`data-tone`/`data-size` (lines 47-56), so `variant="outline"` falls through Vue's default attribute inheritance as a junk literal DOM attribute with ZERO styling effect; the buttons silently render at the DEFAULT `emphasis="secondary"`, `tone="neutral"`. `size="sm"` IS valid (ButtonSize = xs|sm|md|lg), so only the variant limb is dead. I additionally proved the failure is TYPE-INVISIBLE: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` ran to completion with zero diagnostics. SCOPE CORRECTION the axis missed: this is not PaginationBar-local staleness but a repo-wide epidemic — 51 `<Button variant=...>` sites across 20 files (e.g. AdminAuditPanel.vue:30,49; AdminUsersPanel.vue:21,32,58,112,122; ProfileSection.vue:59,111,135; BrowsePane.vue:69,136), while the CORRECT vocabulary is already in use elsewhere (`emphasis="text"` at PalettesPane.vue:113 and AdminUsersPanel.vue:174) — i.e. a partially-completed glass-ui 7 migration, not a one-off.

confirmed.claim: No pending guard prevents double activation; users can repeatedly activate arrows while results load.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED, and the cure is trivially available and unused. `PaginationBar.vue:10,24` bind `:disabled` ONLY to `!hasPrev`/`!hasNext` — there is no busy/pending input at all; the component's prop surface (`:37-42`) has no `loading`. The producer ships the exact affordance: `Button.vue.d.ts:16` `loading?: boolean` — "Marks an in-flight command and suppresses activation until it settles" — implemented at `button-Bu9F4uU6.js:35` (`m = loading || disabled`) with an activation-suppressing handler at `:44`. The in-flight flag is already published by both ports (`demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:39,96` and `demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:52,138` expose `loading`) and is already consumed for skeletons by the panels (AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16), but is never threaded to PaginationBar. Double-activation is executably reproduced in-repo at `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminFlaggedPanel/repro/flagged-composable.test.ts:51-62` ("C2: double-click Next skips a page and leaves two flights in the air" — asserts page lands on 3 and offsets [20,40] are both requested).

confirmed.claim: Events carry no destination/request identity, so parent and child can race; out-of-order responses are possible.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED as to the RACE, but the axis misattributes the cause and therefore prescribes the wrong cure. `PaginationBar.vue:44-47` emits bare `prev`/`next`; handlers are `audit.prevPage`/`nextPage` (AdminAuditPanel.vue:88-89) and `flagged.prevPage`/`nextPage` (AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:131-132). The real defect is in the composables: `useAdminAudit.ts:48-71` and `useAdminFlagged.ts:59-79` carry NO request-sequence token and NO in-flight bail — every `loadX()` unconditionally assigns `entries/items = res.data` and `total = res.total` on resolve, so two overlapping flights resolve last-wins regardless of which page they were for. Also `loading` is a plain boolean, so the `finally` of the FIRST flight (useAdminAudit.ts:68-70) clears `loading` while the second is still airborne, retracting the skeleton early. Executably reproduced in-repo at `docs/.../AdminFlaggedPanel/repro/flagged-composable.test.ts:27-49` ("C1: out-of-order responses — the STALE page wins (no request sequencing)", asserting `page===2` while `items[0].paletteSlug==="page1-row"`). CURE CORRECTION: putting a destination in the emit (the axis's prescription) does not fix this — the child would still be a dumb relay and the stale write would still land. The structurally sound fix is a monotonic request-generation token in the composable, discarding responses whose generation is superseded.

confirmed.claim: `pageCount > 1` is the sole guard; page values outside [1,pageCount] are rendered verbatim.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED ONLY for the `page > pageCount` limb; the other limbs are unreachable (see killed C-1-limbs). `PaginationBar.vue:3` guards solely on `pageCount > 1` and `:18` interpolates `Page {{ page }} of {{ pageCount }}` with no clamp. `page > pageCount` IS reachable in the live tree via the un-clamped local decrement in `useAdminFlagged.ts:87` / `:99` (`total.value = Math.max(0, total.value - 1)` with no page clamp and no reload). Worked example: pageSize 20 (`useAdminFlagged.ts:51`), total 41, page 3 → pageCount = Math.max(1, ceil(41/20)) = 3 (`:55`); dismiss one row → total 40 → pageCount 2 while page stays 3 → the bar renders (2 > 1) and literally reads "Page 3 of 2". Here `hasNext=false`, `hasPrev=true` (`:56-57`) so the user can still escape via Previous — which is why this variant is MAJOR and not the BLOCKER; the unrecoverable sibling case is filed separately under MISSED.

confirmed.claim: aria-live announces page-text mutations that are not bound to completion of the corresponding list request.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED structurally. `PaginationBar.vue:17` marks the counter `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"`, and `:18` renders `page` directly. `useAdminAudit.ts:73-78` (`nextPage`) increments `page.value++` SYNCHRONOUSLY and only then calls the async `loadAuditLog()`; identical shape at `useAdminFlagged.ts:105-110`. Vue flushes the reactive text update on the next microtask tick, long before the network promise resolves, so the region announces "Page 3 of 5" while the panel is still showing the previous page's rows (or, once `loading` flips, skeletons at AdminAuditPanel.vue:36-38). The announcement is therefore bound to intent, not to commit. Severity held to MINOR: announcing navigation intent is a defensible pattern and no false content is spoken — the counter is accurate about the requested page. Whether a real screen reader's queueing makes this audible as a mis-ordering is UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE (no AT available under probe parsimony). Motion/PRM law is not implicated: `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md:274` lists PaginationBar C·D·L under "§7.4 No motion content — vacuously cleared", so no M-xx row constrains any verdict here.

confirmed.claim: There are no first/last or direct-page affordances, and no threshold or large-count design exists.
confirmed.proof: Factually CONFIRMED but NOT a defect at the shipped scale — recorded at INFO to prevent it being carried as remediable. `PaginationBar.vue:7-29` contains exactly three children: prev Button, counter span, next Button. There is no first/last control, no page jump, no ellipsis range. However both consumers page at `pageSize = 20` (`useAdminAudit.ts:38`, `useAdminFlagged.ts:51`) over admin-scale collections (audit ledger, flag queue), and the repo carries an explicit standing edict against speculative structure (MEMORY `feedback_kiss_no_contrivance.md`: "Don't create new shared/ dirs or wrapper components that don't exist yet; KISS"). Building a large-count design for a surface with no evidenced large-count usage would violate that edict. The honest finding is the absence of a documented threshold, not the absence of the controls.

killed.claim: `hasNext`/`hasPrev` are trusted instead of derived, allowing "Page 1 of 2" with Previous enabled or Next disabled; the four scalars can contradict each other.
killed.refutation: REFUTED — the contradiction is unreachable in the live tree, and the axis reached this verdict only because it declared itself "Source-only" (challenge-C-implementation.md:3, challenge-L-library.md:3) and never opened the two files that produce the props. There are exactly two call sites, and BOTH derive all four scalars from the same two numbers. `demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:44-46`: `pageCount = computed(() => Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total.value / pageSize)))`, `hasNext = computed(() => page.value < pageCount.value)`, `hasPrev = computed(() => page.value > 1)`. Byte-identical derivation at `demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:55-57`. These are `computed` refs, not free-floating booleans, so "Page 1 of 2 with Previous enabled" would require `1 > 1` to evaluate true. The bindings are direct (AdminAuditPanel.vue:84-87, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:127-130) with no transformation. The "four unrelated scalars" framing further presumes a library boundary that does not exist: PaginationBar is a PRIVATE component — `grep -rn PaginationBar demo/ --include=*.ts` returns zero hits, and the admin barrel `demo/palettes/browser/admin/index.ts:3-7` exports only the five panels, deliberately ("NAMED re-exports only (PI-6)"). No external caller can supply a contradictory Cartesian product. NOTE: the ONE genuinely reachable inconsistency (page > pageCount) does not arise from untrusted props at all but from the composable's un-clamped delete path — filed as confirmed C-1 and as the MISSED blocker.

killed.claim: `Button` arrives via a forwarding barrel [through a stale axis] — framed as part of the defect.
killed.refutation: REFUTED as a defect. The forwarding barrel is the SANCTIONED, uniform house pattern, not staleness. `demo/ui/button/index.ts` is a one-line `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`, and all 20 sibling primitives follow it identically (`demo/ui/{alert,avatar,badge,card,checkbox,collapsible,dialog,dropdown-menu,input,label,popover,radio-group,select,separator,...}/index.ts`). The pattern is explicitly ruled and documented at `demo/ui/alert/index.ts:1-9`: the barrel "previously held a local shadcn-vue re-implementation ... B.W2 (A.W7 idiomatic-gestalt finding N1) converted it to a re-export: glass-ui is the design system, the demo consumes its Alert, not a hand-rolled copy." This matches the standing edict in MEMORY (`feedback_glass_ui_first_class.md`). PaginationBar.vue:34 consuming `../../../ui/button` is therefore correct and conformant. Only the `variant` limb of this bullet survives (confirmed as L-1); conflating the two would send a fixer to unwind correct architecture.

killed.claim: `page=0`, negative values, or non-integer values are rendered verbatim.
killed.refutation: REFUTED — these three limbs are unreachable. `page` is initialised to `1` (`useAdminAudit.ts:37`, `useAdminFlagged.ts:50`) and the ONLY mutations are `page.value++` behind `if (hasNext.value)` and `page.value--` behind `if (hasPrev.value)` (`useAdminAudit.ts:73-85`, `useAdminFlagged.ts:105-117`), plus a reset to the literal `1` at AdminAuditPanel.vue:114. Since `hasPrev = page > 1` gates every decrement, `page` can never reach 0 or go negative; since every mutation is ±1 from the integer 1, it can never be non-integer. Likewise `pageCount` can never be zero or negative: `Math.max(1, Math.ceil(...))` (`useAdminAudit.ts:44`, `useAdminFlagged.ts:55`) pins it to ≥1 and `Math.ceil` pins it to an integer. Only the `page > pageCount` limb is live (confirmed separately).

killed.claim: The bar disappears whenever `pageCount <= 1`; that conflates a verified single page with unknown count, loading, error, and invalid negative/zero totals.
killed.refutation: REFUTED AS STATED (though it gestures near the real defect). (a) The "invalid negative/zero totals" limb is impossible: `pageCount = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total/pageSize))` (useAdminFlagged.ts:55, useAdminAudit.ts:44) cannot yield ≤0. (b) The loading and error limbs are already discharged by the PANELS, which own dedicated branches: skeletons at AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16-18 / AdminAuditPanel.vue:36-38 and a distinct error EmptyState at AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:22-33 / AdminAuditPanel.vue:42-53, both carrying provenance comments ("W5-5 (F-2, the P0 case): error ≠ empty — a dead backend never costumes as a clear ledger"). Hiding a pagination control when there is exactly one page is standard correct behaviour, not a conflation. (c) The "unknown count" limb is vacuous: `total` is initialised to 0 and only ever assigned from a resolved response, so pre-load state is covered by the loading branch. The genuine harm of the `pageCount > 1` guard is NOT ambiguity of meaning — it is that the guard removes the user's only escape control at the exact moment they need it, which this axis did not see; filed as the MISSED blocker.

killed.claim: The live-region sentence is locally authored; other paginated surfaces can announce at a different phase.
killed.refutation: REFUTED — the premise is counterfactual. There is no other paginated surface to diverge from: PaginationBar.vue is the sole pagination component in the tree (`find demo/ -iname '*pagination*'` returns exactly one file) and it has exactly two consumers, AdminAuditPanel.vue:83-90 and AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:126-133, both of which route through this same component and therefore through this same live region at `PaginationBar.vue:17`. Divergent announcement phase across surfaces is impossible while the component remains the single implementation. The finding describes a risk of a future second implementation, not a live defect. (A real, different a11y defect in this same live region — that it is nested inside the `v-if` and so is absent at mount — is filed under MISSED.)

killed.claim: This generic pattern belongs either in glass-ui or in a shared application collection package, not independently in each admin panel; target a `PaginationState = unknown | ready | loading | error` ADT.
killed.refutation: REFUTED on both limbs. (a) FACTUAL ERROR in the premise: it is NOT implemented "independently in each admin panel" — there is exactly ONE implementation (PaginationBar.vue), imported by both panels (AdminAuditPanel.vue:102, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:144). There is no duplication to extract. (b) The prescribed cure is not structurally supported: glass-ui 7.0.0 ships no Pagination primitive — `ls node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/` lists 60 components and contains none (the nearest, `pager-dots`, is carousel dot-indicators, a different control), so this is not the `feedback_glass_ui_first_class` case of hand-rolling a copy of a shipped primitive. Promoting a 48-line private component with two same-directory consumers into a producer package or inventing a new shared collection package directly contradicts the standing owner edict (MEMORY `feedback_kiss_no_contrivance.md`: "Don't create new shared/ dirs or wrapper components that don't exist yet; KISS"). The ADT target is likewise premature: the component's actual defects (dead `variant`, missing `icon-only`, missing `loading`, un-clamped page) are all fixable in place by using props the producer already ships. Extraction would be motion without remedy.

missed.claim: BLOCKER — the `pageCount > 1` guard removes the ONLY escape control at the exact moment it is needed: emptying the last page of the flag queue permanently strands the admin on a dead page, showing "No flagged palettes." and a nonzero flag count simultaneously, unrecoverable for the session without a browser reload.
missed.proof: All three axes missed this because all three declared themselves "Source-only" and never opened the composables. Exact mechanism, fully static-provable: (1) `demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:86-87` (`dismiss`) and `:98-99` (`deletePalette`) mutate state LOCALLY — `items.value = items.value.filter(...)` and `total.value = Math.max(0, total.value - 1)` — with NO refetch and NO page clamp. (2) `demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:90` and `:98` wire these straight from the template, and the panel's only load is `onMounted(() => flagged.loadFlagged())` at `:152` — nothing reloads after a moderation action. (3) Worked case: pageSize 20 (`useAdminFlagged.ts:51`), total 21, page 2 (one row on the last page). Dismiss it → items `[]`, total 20 → `pageCount = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(20/20)) = 1` (`:55`) while `page` stays 2. (4) `PaginationBar.vue:3` `v-if="pageCount > 1"` is now FALSE → the entire bar, including the Previous button (`:7-15`) that `hasPrev = page > 1` (`:57`) still reports as enabled, is UNMOUNTED. (5) `AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:37-41` renders EmptyState "No flagged palettes." while `:5-7` simultaneously renders "20 flagged" — the panel contradicts itself on screen. (6) The trap is PERMANENT for the session: the Refresh button (`:10`) calls `loadFlagged`, which computes `offset = (page-1)*pageSize = 20` (`:67`) against a 20-item collection and returns empty again, re-confirming pageCount 1; `grep -rn 'page.value = ' demo/palettes/` finds exactly ONE reset in the whole tree — `AdminAuditPanel.vue:114`, which belongs to the AUDIT panel's filter watcher — so `flagged.page` has no reset path at all once the bar is gone. (7) The state is a composition-root singleton (`demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:73` `const flagged = useAdminFlagged()`, provided at `:245`), so it survives panel unmount/remount; only a full page reload clears it. CORROBORATION: an executable repro already exists in a SIBLING component's corpus and explicitly cites this component — `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminFlaggedPanel/repro/flagged-composable.test.ts:64-84`, test "C3: emptying the last page STRANDS the panel — empty list, total>0, pagination bar gone", whose line 72 reads `const paginationBarRendered = f.pageCount.value > 1; // PaginationBar.vue:3 v-if` and asserts `toBe(false)`. So the megatranche already holds proof of this defect, yet ZERO of PaginationBar's three axes carry it. The audit panel is NOT affected (no delete path; its filter watcher resets page to 1), so the blocker is specific to the flag queue. Minimal sound cure: clamp in the composable — after any local decrement, `if (page.value > pageCount.value) page.value = pageCount.value` followed by `loadFlagged()`; the `v-if` guard may stay.

missed.claim: MAJOR — the two icon-only buttons never set the producer's `iconOnly` geometry axis, so they render with text-button padding and forfeit the shipped square-target/hit-area treatment, despite the repo using the correct prop elsewhere.
missed.proof: The L axis found the dead `variant` but stopped there and missed the affirmative prop that IS required. `PaginationBar.vue:7-15` and `:21-29` render Buttons whose sole child is an icon (`<ChevronLeft class="h-4 w-4">` / `<ChevronRight ...>`), with `aria-label` supplied — i.e. textbook icon-only commands. The producer ships a dedicated axis for exactly this: `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:17` — `iconOnly?: boolean` — "Square geometry for an accessibly named icon command." The compiled component consumes it at `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js:52-53`, emitting `data-icon-only` and, notably, `data-control-target` (the hit-target hook) ONLY when set. PaginationBar sets neither, so both attributes are absent and the buttons fall to default non-square geometry. This is not a speculative API: the repo already uses the kebab template form correctly in comparable icon buttons — `demo/palettes/browser/slug/PaletteSlugBar.vue:20` and `:32`, `demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:65`, `demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:166` and `:176` (21 `icon-only` occurrences across demo/). Same root cause as L-1: an incomplete glass-ui 7 migration, invisible to `vue-tsc` (demo typecheck ran clean) because the prop is optional. Cure is one attribute per button, no structural change.

missed.claim: MINOR — the `aria-live` region is nested INSIDE the `v-if`, so it is created together with its first content and destroyed/recreated on every pageCount 1↔2 transition; a live region must pre-exist its mutations to announce reliably.
missed.proof: Missed by C-5 and D-4, which both reasoned only about announcement TIMING relative to the request, never about region LIFETIME. `PaginationBar.vue:2-3` opens the wrapper `<div v-if="pageCount > 1">` and the live region at `:17` (`aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"`) sits inside it, closing at `:30`. Consequence: when a collection grows from one page to two, the region is inserted into the accessibility tree already populated with "Page 1 of 2" — assistive tech generally does not announce content present at region-creation time, only subsequent mutations — so the transition into a paginated state is silent. Symmetrically, when pageCount drops to 1 the region is torn out of the DOM, which is also the mechanism of the BLOCKER above. Ordinary page-to-page stepping (region already mounted, text mutates) does announce correctly, which is why this is MINOR rather than MAJOR. Whether a specific screen reader suppresses the mount-time content is UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE under probe parsimony; the DOM lifetime itself is statically certain. Cure: hoist the live region outside the `v-if` (or swap `v-if` for `v-show` on the wrapper) so the region is stable for the panel's lifetime.

missed.claim: INFO — the megatranche's own executable repro/probe tests live under `docs/` and fall OUTSIDE the vitest include globs, so none of them are ever executed by the suite; the audit program's evidence cannot regress-guard the defects it proves.
missed.proof: Discovered while attempting to execute the corroborating repro. `vitest.config.ts:21` sets `include: ["test/**/*.ts", "demo/test/**/*.ts"]`. The audit evidence lives elsewhere: `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminFlaggedPanel/repro/flagged-composable.test.ts`, `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminAuditPanel/pi/probe.test.ts`, `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/VersionHistoryDrawer/evidence-C2/vhd-probes.test.ts`. Running `npx vitest run docs/.../flagged-composable.test.ts` returns "No test files found, exiting with code 1" with vitest echoing the include globs. These files are well-built (proper mocks, deferred promises, explicit assertions) and encode real proven defects — including the BLOCKER above — yet they are inert: they will neither fail when a defect is reintroduced nor break when the composable API drifts, and they use absolute `/Users/mkbabb/...` mock paths (flagged-composable.test.ts:10-17) that would not survive relocation as-is. Note this is an observation about the audit corpus's durability, not a product defect; recorded because my lens is code/contract health and because a fixer landing the BLOCKER cure would otherwise have no regression gate available.

missed.claim: INFO — all three axes audited a props-only leaf "Source-only" and never read the two files that produce its props, which is the common root cause of every false finding above and of the missed BLOCKER.
missed.proof: Method finding, offered to calibrate future re-reads rather than as a product defect. Each axis states the restriction in its own receipt: `challenge-C-implementation.md:3` ("Source-only."), `challenge-D-design.md:5` ("Source-only."), `challenge-L-library.md:3` ("Static audit only."). PaginationBar.vue is 48 lines with zero internal state — `defineProps` at `:37-42`, `defineEmits` at `:44-47` — so essentially all of its behaviour is determined by `demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts` and `demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts`, neither of which any axis cites. The measurable cost: three findings assert contradictions among the four props that the derivations at useAdminAudit.ts:44-46 / useAdminFlagged.ts:55-57 make arithmetically impossible (killed C-2/L-2, C-1-limbs), one asserts duplication across panels that does not exist (killed L-5), one asserts sibling paginated surfaces that do not exist (killed L-4) — while the one genuinely severe, session-permanent, user-trapping defect lives 30 lines into a file none of them opened. For a props-only leaf, the caller set is not context, it is the specification.

unproven: UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE — whether a real screen reader audibly announces the counter mutation BEFORE the corresponding rows commit (confirmed C-5/D-4). The DOM/reactivity ordering is statically certain (useAdminAudit.ts:73-78 increments synchronously, then awaits), but actual AT queueing/coalescing behaviour requires live assistive technology, which probe parsimony and the no-browser-tooling law forbid here.

UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE — whether a screen reader suppresses the mount-time content of the `v-if`-nested live region (missed MINOR). The region's DOM lifetime is statically proven from PaginationBar.vue:2-3/17/30; the announcement outcome is an AT-behaviour question.

UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE — D-5's hedged limb that "the visual hierarchy may not match the source." I proved the mechanism statically (variant is inert; buttons fall back to emphasis="secondary"/tone="neutral" per button-Bu9F4uU6.js:11-12,47-56), but whether the resulting rendered weight is actually wrong for this surface is a rendered-pixel judgement requiring a live view.

NOT ASSESSED — cross-browser/forced-colors and touch hit-target sizing for the two chevron buttons. Relevant because the missing `iconOnly` also suppresses `data-control-target` (button-Bu9F4uU6.js:53), but measuring the resulting hit area needs live layout.
superlatives: EXCELLENT — the `demo/ui/*` barrel discipline is a genuinely well-executed architectural decision, and it is self-documenting. `demo/ui/alert/index.ts:1-9` carries the full rationale and provenance in-line ("This barrel previously held a local shadcn-vue re-implementation ... B.W2 (A.W7 idiomatic-gestalt finding N1) converted it to a re-export: glass-ui is the design system"), and all 20 sibling primitives conform to the same one-line re-export shape. A reader can recover both the rule and the ruling that produced it without leaving the file. The L axis mistook this for a defect.

EXCELLENT — the icon-button accessibility idiom in PaginationBar is exactly right and is the paired form most codebases get wrong: `aria-label` on the interactive element (`PaginationBar.vue:11`, `:25`) AND `aria-hidden="true"` on the decorative icon inside it (`:14`, `:28`), so the accessible name is spoken once with no icon-node noise. It carries its provenance comment at `:6` ("W5-a11y: icon-only pagination buttons need aria-labels"). The same discipline is applied consistently across the admin cluster (AdminAuditPanel.vue:29-31, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:9-11, :97,:100).

EXCELLENT — `tabular-nums` on the page counter (`PaginationBar.vue:17`) is a precise, easily-forgotten typographic choice: it pins digit advance width so the counter does not reflow as page numbers change width (1→10→100), keeping the flanking chevrons visually static. Paired correctly with `aria-atomic="true"` so the counter is announced as one sentence rather than as two mutated numbers.

EXCELLENT (producer-side) — glass-ui 7.0.0's axis vocabulary is unusually disciplined API design, and it explicitly anticipates precisely the mistake this component makes. `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/_shared/axes.d.ts:16` documents the tone axis as "the semantic status register (`--<tone>` token cohort); NEVER a `variant` member" — the producer names and forbids the collapsed-variant anti-pattern in the type declaration itself. `Button.vue.d.ts:8-18` follows through with orthogonal `emphasis` (visual priority, "It does not change the command's semantics") vs `tone` (semantic intent), each documented at the property.

EXCELLENT — the `loadError` discipline in both composables is a textbook correct error posture, and rare: `useAdminAudit.ts:63-67` and `useAdminFlagged.ts:71-75` clear the error on success and populate it on failure, and the panels render a genuinely distinct error branch ahead of the empty branch (AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:22-33 before :37-41). The provenance comments state the invariant crisply — "W5-5 (F-2, the P0 case): error ≠ empty — a dead backend never costumes as a clear ledger" — which is exactly the failure mode most list UIs ship. Note this makes the flag queue's SILENT dismiss/delete failures (useAdminFlagged.ts:88-90, :100-102, console.warn only) an inconsistency with the surrounding standard rather than an absence of one.

EXCELLENT — PaginationBar is correctly scoped as a small, private, single-purpose leaf: 48 lines, no internal state, modern typed `defineEmits<{ prev: []; next: [] }>()` tuple syntax (`:44-47`), typed `defineProps` (`:37-42`), and deliberately withheld from the public barrel (`demo/palettes/browser/admin/index.ts:1-7`, "NAMED re-exports only (PI-6)"). Its defects are all one-line prop omissions; none are structural. This is the right size and the right visibility for what it does.
